Group the events by variables from the metadata

Source: R/group_by_meta.R
group_by_meta.Rd

This function groups the events of a move2 object by one or more variables of the track metadata (e.g. the sex of each animal), for example to estimate a home range for each group with the hr_tt_*() functions, which return the grouping variables as columns. It is the counterpart of filter_by_meta() for dplyr::group_by(), and it replaces move2::group_by_track_data(), so that it also works with locations in the metadata.

Usage

group_by_meta(
  .data,
  ...,
  .add = FALSE,
  .drop = dplyr::group_by_drop_default(.data)
)

Arguments

.data

A move2 object

...

Variables of the track metadata to group by, or new variables computed from them (as in dplyr::group_by())

.add

When FALSE (the default), the new groups replace any existing groups; when TRUE, they are added to them (as in dplyr::group_by())

.drop

Whether to drop the groups formed by levels of factors that do not appear in the data (as in dplyr::group_by())

Value

A grouped move2 object, with the grouping variables moved from the metadata to the events

Details

To group the events, the grouping variables are moved from the metadata to the events (as as_event_column() does), so that the only column in both tables is the track id. They stay in the events after dplyr::ungroup(), and can be moved back with as_meta_column(); to group again by variables that are already in the events, use dplyr::group_by(). A column of the events with the name of a grouping variable is kept if it has the same values as in the metadata (e.g. the id of each animal after tt_split_trips()); otherwise, an error is raised.

The grouping variables are evaluated on the metadata, so they can also be new variables computed from its columns (e.g. north = nest_lat > 0), as in dplyr::group_by(); the columns used to compute them stay in the metadata.

Locations in the metadata (e.g. of a colony), stored as sfc columns (see sf_point_col()), can be grouping variables, and are moved to the events as sfc columns; the events keep their own geometry. An sf table of metadata is turned into a plain table first, with its geometry kept as an sfc column, which is renamed if it has the name of the geometry column of the events (see show_meta()).

See also

filter_by_meta() to filter the tracks by variables of the metadata, and as_event_column() and as_meta_column() to move variables between the metadata and the events.

Examples

# group the events by the sex of each animal
sex_tt <- example_tt %>% group_by_meta(sex)
dplyr::group_keys(sex_tt)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 1
#>   sex   
#>   <chr> 
#> 1 female
#> 2 male  
# sex has been moved from the metadata to the events
show_meta(sex_tt)
#>   track_id nest_lon nest_lat
#> 1        a     1.37     0.06
#> 2        b    -2.44    -1.76
#> 3        c    -0.78     0.43

# group by a new variable computed from the metadata
example_tt %>%
  group_by_meta(nest_north = nest_lat > 0) %>%
  dplyr::group_keys()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 1
#>   nest_north
#>   <lgl>     
#> 1 FALSE     
#> 2 TRUE      

# group by the locations of the nests, stored as an sfc column of the
# metadata
nests_tt <- example_tt
show_meta(nests_tt)$nest <- sf_point_col(
  x = show_meta(nests_tt)$nest_lon,
  y = show_meta(nests_tt)$nest_lat,
  crs = 4326
)
nests_tt %>%
  group_by_meta(nest) %>%
  dplyr::group_keys()
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>            nest
#>     <POINT [°]>
#> 1   (1.37 0.06)
#> 2 (-2.44 -1.76)
#> 3  (-0.78 0.43)
